newsitem.title: USA: Horry Cty, Myrtle Beach, S.C. mull $11 mln arena.
newsitem.headline: Horry Cty, Myrtle Beach, S.C. mull $11 mln arena.

text.p: South Carolina's Horry County and City of Myrtle Beach governments are in discussions with the owners of the Durham Bulls to build an $11 million stadium for the baseball farm team, the Sun News reported Friday.
Capital Broadcasting Inc, which owns the Bulls, has asked the city and county to pay $5 million each, with the company paying $1 million plus any cost overruns.
A Myrtle Beach company, Burroughs & Chapin Co Inc, would donate land for the stadium in exchange for exclusive rights to use it 23 days a year.

The Bulls currently play in Durham, N.C. and are a farm team for the Atlanta Braves. They would move to South Carolina and be renamed the Myrtle Beach Braves if the deal goes through, the newspaper said.
The county and county councils could vote on the proposal as early as Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted a team attorney as saying the owners would rather move the Bulls to South Carolina. But it said the team could alternatively move to York County, Va., where six local governments will vote over the next few weeks on a proposal to build a $12.5 million stadium for the Bulls.
If that deal is approved, the Bulls could be bought by Ken Young, who already owns the Norfolk Tides farm team for the New York Mets, the newspaper said.
